title: Field-tuned quasiparticles and electronic structure in heavy-fermion YbNi4P2
authors: Will Broad, Owen Moulding, Takaki Muramatsu, Manuel Brando, Alix McCollam, Femke Bangman, Gertrud Zwicknagl, Kristin Kliemt, Cornelius Krellner, Sven Friedemann
abstract: We study the Fermi surface topology and quasiparticle properties in the heavy fermion compound YbNi4P2 at high magnetic fields using quantum oscillation measurements. We observe a large decrease of the quasiparticle mass with increasing field and demonstrate good qualitative agreement with the single-ion Kondo model. At the putative Lifshitz transition at 17 T, we observe a sudden change of quantum oscillation frequencies suggesting an abrupt change of the electronic structure and/or quasiparticle characteristics. Our results demonstrate the ability to tune the electronic structure and provide input for theoretical models of YbNi4P2 and correlated electron systems in high magnetic fields.
summary: This paper uses quantum oscillation measurements on the heavy-fermion compound YbNi4P2 to probe its electronic structure under high magnetic fields. Key findings include observing a field-dependent renormalization of the quasiparticle mass and detecting an abrupt change in quantum oscillation frequencies at a critical field. This suggests that external magnetic fields can tune the electronic structure, providing crucial input for theoretical models of correlated electron systems.
main_problem: The study investigates the electronic structure and quasiparticle properties in the heavy-fermion compound YbNi4P2 under the influence of high magnetic fields.
main_result: The research observes a field-dependent decrease in quasiparticle mass and detects an abrupt change in quantum oscillation frequencies at a critical field (17 T), suggesting a field-induced electronic structure transition.
method: The primary method involves performing quantum oscillation (QO) measurements on magnetoresistance and its derivative, complemented by fitting temperature dependence to extract effective mass.
model_or_system: The physical system is the heavy-fermion compound YbNi4P2, characterized by strong electronic correlations arising from the hybridization of local moments and conduction electrons. The analysis compares experimental results to predictions from the single-ion Kondo model.
key_observables: Quantum oscillation frequencies (F), quasiparticle effective mass (m*), Sommerfeld coefficient (gamma_S), and magnetoresistance R(B).
important_parameters: High magnetic fields (up to 35 T), the critical field B9 (17 T), and the characteristic energy scale of the Kondo effect.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the observed phenomena can be modeled by the single-ion Kondo model and that the abrupt frequency changes signal a Lifshitz transition or electronic structure change.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate QO signals across different field orientations, the field-dependence of the effective mass (showing splitting above B9), and the abrupt change in oscillation frequencies at the critical field B9.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes QO data, first establishing the field-dependence of the quasiparticle mass relative to the Kondo model, then pinpointing the critical field B9 where frequency splitting occurs, and finally discussing the implications for Fermi surface topology.
why_interesting: The study provides experimental evidence of field-tuning of electronic structure in a strongly correlated material, offering insights into how external fields can drive quantum phase transitions in heavy fermion systems, which is relevant to understanding correlated quantum matter.

FIG. 2. Field-dependence of quasiparticle mass. (a) Background-subtracted derivative of the resistance in the field range B4 < B < B7 (cf. Table S2). (b) Effective masses extracted from Lifshitz-Kosevich (LK) fits (Figure S2) as a function of magnetic field for Fγ below B9 and for F ± γ above B9. Horizontal (grey) bars denote the field range over which the mass was extracted. Vertical bars denote standard errors from LK fits. Yellow squares show the field dependence of the Sommerfeld coefficient [14] on separate axis (right). Solid blue line shows the de-renormalisation of the quasiparticle mass for a single-ion Kondo model with the parameters relevant for YbNi4P2 (see text for details).

Labels indicate assigned frequencies.
